code_vs_mdcalc.issue: PaO2 gap: code uses 61<=PaO2<=70 ->1 and 55<=PaO2<=60 ->3, so a non-integer PaO2 between 60 and 61 falls to the else branch and scores 4 (should be 3 or 1).

A-a gradient gap: 200<=A-a<=349 ->2 and 350<=A-a<=499 ->3, so a non-integer value between 349 and 350 falls to else and scores 0 (should be 2-3). Top band uses >499 (MDCalc/Knaus >=500), equivalent for integers.
Age bands use closed integer ranges (45<=age<=54 etc.), so non-integer ages in (54,55), (64,65), (74,75) match no branch and score 0.

MAP bands written as 129<MAP<=159 etc.; for non-integer MAP in (129,130), (109,110), (69,70), (49,50) the code assigns the higher-risk-side band differently from MDCalc's integer bands. No row has a MAP in these windows (MAPs range 84.7-120.0).

Creatinine: code adds a 'chronic_renal_failure' input that MDCalc does not have. With CRF=True and creatinine <1.5 the CRF branch adds 0 and the no-renal-failure branch is skipped, so creatinine <0.6 scores 0 instead of 2. With ARF=True and creatinine <0.6 the code scores 0 instead of doubled 4 (Knaus doubles the creatinine score). For creatinine >=1.5 the CRF branch gives the same points as no ARF, matching MDCalc. All CRF/ARF rows have creatinine >=1.5.

organ_failure_or_immunocompromise=True with surgery_type missing or unrecognized adds 0 points (MDCalc would require a type; nonoperative default = 5). All rows with organ failure True have a surgery type.

MDCalc takes creatinine in umol/L; code bands in mg/dL. Converted MDCalc umol/L cutpoints can differ by a few hundredths of a mg/dL at band edges (e.g. ~1.47-1.49, ~1.92-1.99, ~3.45-3.49 mg/dL). No row has a creatinine in these windows.
